key_insight: Collective vortex escape in a pinned, spinning-down superfluid weakens boundary flow until the escape self-arrests, limiting angular momentum transfer to the container.
engineering_relevance: The findings identify how pinning thresholds, container size, and initial rotation can constrain sudden angular momentum transfer in rotating superfluid systems.
method: Analyze collective vortex migration in a spinning-down container with pinning centres.
Identify the minimum opening angle of a near-wall vacated sector associated with the first vortex exodus.
Relate boundary-flow weakening and depletion-region dimensions to self-arrest.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a minimum-angle onset condition and well-defined depletion-region dimensions, but provides no quantitative results or evaluation details.
watch_item: Relevance to pulsar glitches is discussed, but the abstract does not establish validation under neutron-star conditions.
paper_title: Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids
